issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: 'Risky Behavior' is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which otherwise emphasizes hypervigilance, startle, danger in silence, fragmented/avoided trauma memory, and appraisals of betrayal and injustice after police violence. Those other items describe a fearful, threat-sensitive presentation; endorsing active risk-taking as a core threat item pulls in the opposite direction and is not supported elsewhere in the selected nodes.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Can't Rely on Self: I can't rely on myself
issues.explanation: 'Can't Rely on Self' is a weaker fit than the other appraisals for this trauma/context. The profile is organized around external betrayal/injustice linked to police violence, but this item shifts to global self-distrust without corresponding self-blame, shame, incompetence, or strategy items elsewhere. In combination with the strong betrayal/injustice theme, it creates a less coherent appraisal profile.

vignette: Carlos Carlos, a 54-year-old Latin American parole officer, has been haunted by his experience of police violence for over two years. The traumatic event occurred during what was meant to be a routine traffic stop. Carlos had pulled over a suspected drug dealer when he was suddenly confronted by several officers in full riot gear. They accused him of misconduct and violently arrested him without any provocation. This event left Carlos feeling violated and betrayed, an experience that has since shaped his daily life. The memory of the incident is fragmented and incomplete. Whenever Carlos tries to recall it, he finds himself pushing the details away before they can fully surface, leaving gaps in his recollection. The moments that do emerge feel surreal, making him question whether it really happened to him. This lack of clarity adds to his distress, as he struggles with a sense of disbelief and confusion. Carlos's work as a parole officer has become increasingly difficult due to the trauma. On the job, even small triggers like people misbehaving or his own heart racing can send him into a state of heightened alertness. The unusual silence in courtrooms or during interviews makes him feel that something dangerous is about to happen, and he constantly scans his surroundings for any signs of danger. These reactions are not just fleeting; they have become a persistent part of his daily routine. What frightens Carlos most is the feeling of betrayal by those he trusted. He was certain that the police officers who attacked him were supposed to uphold justice, yet they violated that trust in an act that felt deeply unfair and unjustified. This sense of betrayal has only deepened as time has passed, given that no action has been taken against those responsible for his treatment. The injustice he experienced has also led Carlos to feel like the institutions meant to protect him have failed him completely. He is acutely aware that the memory of this event remains incomplete and unreal, reinforcing his negative appraisals. His constant fear that something dangerous will happen in moments of silence or sudden movements exacerbates these feelings, creating a cycle where each trigger reinforces both his threat perception and his sense of betrayal. Carlos’s daily life has become an intricate dance around these triggers. At work, he avoids situations that might remind him of the event, such as certain neighborhoods or types of cases. This avoidance has strained his relationships with colleagues who do not understand his sudden withdrawal from tasks he once handled with ease. His marriage is also affected; his wife finds it difficult to comprehend why he seems so anxious and on edge all the time. The accumulation of these experiences over time has made Carlos feel increasingly isolated and overwhelmed. He finally sought help when a minor incident at work—a loud noise—sent him into such an intense state of anxiety that he felt unable to continue his job effectively without support. What he hopes for is a sense of normalcy and the ability to trust again, both in himself and in the institutions he once believed in. Carlos’s current state is one of deep turmoil, where each trigger reinforces his threat perception and negative appraisals, making it increasingly difficult for him to function normally. He needs help to break this cycle and regain a sense of safety and justice in his life.
